sections.executive_summary:
Florida group homes for people with developmental disabilities are **licensed by the Agency for Persons with Disabilities (APD)** as *group home facilities* (4–15 residents) or *foster care facilities* (up to 3 residents) under s. 393.067, F.S. and chapter 65G-2, F.A.C. [S7][S8][S30]. They are paid mainly through **residential habilitation** under the **iBudget Florida 1915(c) waiver**, billed to Florida Medicaid at fixed state rates from the iBudget provider rate table (Rule 59G-13.081) [S1][S2]. APD waiver provider enrollment is free [S21], and no license fee appears on the December 2025 license application [S20]; confirm with your APD regional office.

**How the money works.** Rates are set by the resident's *support level* (Basic, Minimal, Moderate, Extensive 1, Extensive 2), by service type (standard, behavioral focus, intensive behavioral) and by county group — not by home size [S1]. A Moderate resident earns **$5,058.37/month** outside South Florida and $5,437.98 in Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach (rates effective Oct. 1, 2025, unchanged since July 1, 2024) [S1][S4]. A July 2026 table with a uniform increase of about 1.0% is in rulemaking [S3][S55]. The rate excludes room and board, which the resident pays from SSI; APD's room-and-board standard is $583.42/month [S5][S26]. Each support level carries a **minimum number of direct-care staff hours per resident per day** (Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11) [S5]. The rates work out to roughly $28 per required staff hour, so profit depends on keeping staffing near the minimum the residents actually need, paying near-market wages and spreading overhead across enough beds.

**Demand.** 37,645 people were enrolled in Florida's DD waivers on June 1, 2026, and 15,451 were in pre-enrollment (the waiting list) on July 1, 2026 [S24]. In June 2026, 6,639 people billed monthly residential habilitation, plus 1,850 behavioral-focus and 873 intensive-behavior day-rate users (APD notes these counts are incomplete) [S24].

**Bottom line.** With one staff on duty 24/7 per home plus handbook-minimum hours, Florida median aide wages ($16.25) and 93% occupancy, a 3-person foster home on the Live-In rate and a 4-bed home lose money, a 6-bed home loses about $1,100/month, and **8-bed homes earn about $1,250–$1,950/month each; two 8-bed homes earn about $2,860/month (3.4%)**. Margins are thin: every $1/hour of DSP wage costs the two-home model about $3,300/month. Because one staff member must be on duty around the clock from the first admission, every configuration loses money in year 1; the two-home model loses about $80,000 in year 1 if both homes open together. Homes of 7–14 residents must sit in multifamily zoning and can be denied by the local government (s. 419.001) [S25], so site selection is the critical early risk.
sections.service_model:
### Program names and license categories
Florida law defines three APD-licensed residential facility types, but only two are open to new applicants [S7]:

| Type | Capacity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Foster care facility | No more than 3 residents | Family living environment; with a live-in caregiver it is not a "community residential home" and is exempt from local zoning notification [S7][S20] |
| Group home facility | At least 4, not more than 15 residents | The standard DD group home [S7] |
| Residential habilitation center | Not fewer than 9 residents | Not available to new applicants — no new licenses since 10/1/1989 (s. 393.063(35)) [S7] |

"Residential habilitation" is the service — supervision and training to acquire, retain or improve daily living, homemaking and social skills so the person can live in the community [S7][S5]. APD will not fund services in an unlicensed facility (s. 393.067(14)) [S8].

### Who is served
People APD has found eligible with a developmental disability: intellectual disability, cerebral palsy, autism, spina bifida, Down syndrome, Phelan-McDermid syndrome or Prader-Willi syndrome, manifesting before age 18 [S7]. Each resident's iBudget plan, developed with a Waiver Support Coordinator, authorizes the service, support level and units [S5].

### Service tiers
- **Standard residential habilitation** — Basic, Minimal, Moderate, Extensive 1, Extensive 2, assigned from APD's Residential Habilitation Rate Descriptors (functional, behavioral and physical needs) [S1].
- **Behavioral focus** — for residents with documented serious behaviors in the past 12 months (injury requiring medical attention, arrest, property damage over $500, restraint or Baker Act, inappropriate sexual behavior). Only in homes APD designates as behavior focus, with behavior-analyst monitoring and ABA-trained staff [S5].
- **Intensive behavioral** (Levels 1–6) and **enhanced intensive behavioral** — eligibility and level set by the APD regional behavior analyst (IB Matrix), designated homes only [S1][S5].
- **Live-In** — a daily rate for homes licensed for three or fewer; staff need not live in the home [S1][S5].

Providers enrolled after January 1, 2015 must be the owner or operator of the licensed facility in which they provide residential habilitation [S5].

### Regulatory framework
- **Licensing:** APD regional offices under ch. 65G-2 (most rules amended March 26, 2026) [S30].
- **Medicaid:** AHCA enrolls providers and pays claims; the rate table and handbook are AHCA rules 59G-13.081 and 59G-13.070 [S2][S6].
- **Federal:** CMS 1915(c) waiver rules and the HCBS settings rule (lease-like protections, privacy, choice of roommate, access to food and visitors) for provider-owned settings [S47].
- **Not DOH:** the Department of Health states that it does **not** inspect APD-licensed homes [S28].
sections.licensing_pathway:
Opening a funded home takes two parallel tracks: an **APD facility license** for the house, and **iBudget waiver provider enrollment** (APD, then AHCA Medicaid) for the business. The provider of residential habilitation must own or operate the licensed home [S5].

### Track A — APD facility license (per home)
1. **Secure the home first.** APD asks applicants to have the home secured before requesting an application, then contacts you for an interview [S22]. Each home needs its own license (65G-2.002(8)) [S9].
2. **Check siting.** Homes of six or fewer residents are a single-family use and need no local approval unless within 1,000 ft of another such home or 1,200 ft of a community residential home. Homes of 7–14 must be in multifamily zoning; the local government has 60 days to approve or deny, and may deny within 1,200 ft of another community residential home or 500 ft of single-family zoning (s. 419.001) [S25]. APD also allows no more than three facilities within 1,000 ft (65G-2.015(4)) [S18]. Follow the five zoning-notification steps in the application (lists of nearby AHCA, DCF and APD homes to local zoning) [S20].
3. **Meet physical standards** (65G-2.007): max two residents per bedroom (homes licensed on/after 7/1/2014); 80 sq ft single / 60 sq ft per person shared; one toilet, sink and tub/shower per three residents; 35 sq ft of living/dining space per household member; hot water ≤120°F; smoke and CO detectors; no mobile homes [S13].
4. **Background screening.** Applicant, managers, supervisors and every direct service staff member complete Level 2 screening through the Clearinghouse before licensure, with a signed affidavit (s. 393.067(5)) [S8][S48].
5. **Fire inspection and CEMP.** Get an approved fire inspection under ch. 69A-38 before the initial license and each renewal (65G-2.010(2)) [S17], and prepare a comprehensive emergency management plan, updated annually (s. 393.067(8)) [S8][S17].
6. **Submit Form 65G-2.002-A (December 2025)** with: articles of organization; staff numbers, experience and training; marketing materials; the lease; fire inspection; CEMP; evidence of financial ability (bank statements, line of credit); the Annual Budget Sheet; behavioral-intervention and sexual-activity policies; floor plan; admission/termination criteria; zoning documentation; and video-monitoring criteria if used [S20]. No license fee appears on the form [S20].
7. **Completeness and inspection.** The application is complete only with all documents, screening results and a satisfactory inspection; APD will not schedule the licensure inspection until documents and screenings are in (65G-2.002(11)-(12)); deficiencies must be fixed before the license issues (65G-2.002(9)) [S9]. APD reviews applications under s. 120.60, F.S. [S9].
8. **License issued for one year** (65G-2.003) [S10]. APD reviews the home on site within 30 days after the first admission (65G-2.0032(8)) [S11] and monitors licensed homes at least monthly, including one weekend visit a year [S22]. Renewals are due at least 45 days before expiration (65G-2.002(4)) [S9].

### Track B — iBudget waiver provider enrollment (per business)
1. Review the handbook qualifications for residential habilitation [S21][S5].
2. Send the Clearinghouse access request (Letter of Intent) to your region's Intent mailbox; register in the Clearinghouse 5–10 business days later; get fingerprinted by a Livescan vendor [S21][S23].
3. After screening clears, submit the APD iBudget provider application with the agency checklist documents and policies to the regional provider enrollment specialist; all checklist documents must go in at once and packets are reviewed in the order received [S21][S23].
4. APD issues a draft **iBudget Provider Service Listing Letter** [S21].
5. Apply to Florida Medicaid through the Medicaid Provider Enrollment Wizard, uploading the listing letter; on approval AHCA sends a Welcome Letter with your Medicaid provider ID [S21]. The CY 2026 federal application fee is $750 where it applies — confirm [S46].
6. Send the Welcome Letter to APD and sign the **Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement (AHCA Form 5000-3553)** [S21][S6].
7. Bill only after Waiver Support Coordinators issue service authorizations [S21]. Behavior focus and intensive behavior also require APD regional designation [S5].

APD publishes no processing time for either track; budget several months and carry rent from the day you sign.
sections.reimbursement:
### Payer and flow
Residential habilitation is a 1915(c) iBudget waiver service. Providers bill Florida Medicaid using the procedure codes in the iBudget rate table, incorporated in Rule 59G-13.081 [S1][S2]. Rates are fixed by the state — there is no managed care negotiation for these codes in the rate table or handbook [S1][S5]. Each resident has an individual iBudget allocation; the Waiver Support Coordinator authorizes the residential habilitation level and units [S5].

### Rate structure (effective Oct. 1, 2025)
- **Monthly vs daily:** a resident in the home 24 or more days bills the monthly rate; fewer days bill the daily rate (max 23); billing waits until the month is complete and no date may be billed when the resident was absent [S1][S5].
- **Support level** sets the rate: Minimal $3,370.96, Moderate $5,058.37, Extensive 1 $6,804.27, Extensive 2 $8,938.77 per month (agency, non-geographical) [S1].
- **Geography:** Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach ("Geographical") pay about 7.5% more (Moderate $5,437.98); Monroe more still ($6,070.04) [S1].
- **Behavioral focus** pays about 4–5% more than standard (Moderate $5,291.07; Extensive 1 $7,117.10) [S1]; **intensive behavioral** pays $363.57–$545.35/day statewide [S1].
- **Home size does not change the rate**, except that the Live-In daily rate ($140.14/day at 1:3, agency, non-geographical) is limited to homes licensed for three or fewer [S1].
- Rates were unchanged from July 1, 2024 [S4]. The July 2026 table (about +1.0%) is in rule development [S3].

### What the rate covers and excludes
The rate includes incidental transportation and documentation time; it excludes room and board, facility upkeep (except safety modifications) and payments to immediate family [S5]. Transportation between the home and another waiver service is paid separately only if you enroll as a transportation provider [S5]. Residential nursing (RN $8.08, LPN $7.02 per 15 minutes) is billable with a prescription [S1].

### Room and board
Residents pay room and board from their own benefits. The facility, if representative payee, must leave a personal needs allowance of at least 18% of the SSI federal benefit rate — $178.92 in 2026 (65G-2.018; SSI $994) [S19][S43]. APD's room-and-board standard is **$583.42/month**: APD pays the full amount for residents under 22 and the shortfall for adults whose benefits net of the PNA fall below it (Rule 65G-13.008; Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days of month end) [S26][S27].

### Revenue per resident in the model
Weighted residential habilitation rate plus $583.42 room and board: about **$5,656/month** for a Minimal/Moderate/Extensive 1 mix of 1:2:1 (non-geographical) and **$6,788** for a behavior-focus Moderate/Extensive 1 mix.
sections.demand:
### Size of the program (APD, FY 2025-26 Q4) [S24]
- **Enrolled:** 37,645 people in Florida's DD waivers on June 1, 2026 (32,316 iBudget + 5,329 CDC+).
- **Waiting list:** 15,451 people in pre-enrollment on July 1, 2026 (Categories 3–7); Categories 1 and 2 (crisis and foster-care-related) are offered enrollment immediately.
- **New enrollments FY 2025-26:** 2,819 (1,091 Category 1, 84 Category 2, 1,590 Categories 3–6, 54 other).
- **Residential habilitation users (June 2026):** 6,639 monthly residential habilitation; 1,850 behavioral focus (day); 873 intensive behavior (day); 279 in ALFs. APD says counts are incomplete because of unsubmitted claims.
- **Spending:** $875.2 million in FY 2025-26 actual expenditures ($943.1 million with AHCA actuals) against a $973.8 million appropriation.

### Referral sources
- **Waiver Support Coordinators** — they authorize services and help residents choose providers [S5][S7].
- **APD regional offices** — crisis placements (Category 1) and residents moving from other settings; region pages list critical needs [S21].
- **Families and guardians**, school transition teams for 18–22-year-olds (APD pays full room and board under 22) [S26].
- **Behavior-focus/intensive referrals** come through the APD regional behavior analyst, who determines eligibility [S5].

### What this means
Demand exists — about 15,000 people waiting and thousands of current residential habilitation users — but placements depend on iBudget enrollment and each person's budget allocation. New homes fill through relationships with support coordinators and APD regional staff, not public advertising. This report does not claim a regional shortage or surplus of beds; no official count of licensed homes was found.
sections.operations:
### Staffing rules
- **One staff present at all times** while residents are in the home, unless APD approves a written plan for a specific resident to be alone for limited periods (65G-2.009(6)(b)) [S16].
- **Handbook minimum direct-care hours per resident per 24-hour day:** Basic 2, Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11. Multiply by residents at each level for the home's daily minimum; meet it daily or over a seven-day period. Example: six Moderate residents = 36 hours/day, 252 hours/week [S5]. Staffing must exceed the minimum when residents need more [S5][S15].
- **Facility operator** on site or on call at all times, with a designated backup; 90 college credits in a related field, or a high school diploma plus three years of disability experience (65G-2.0072) [S14].
- **Direct service providers:** 18+, high school diploma/GED, Level 2 screening, and one year of relevant experience or 30 semester hours/720 classroom hours of related training; new staff without experience can work under 90 days of direct supervision with APD notice within 5 days (65G-2.008(2)) [S15].
- **Behavior focus:** BCBA or Ch. 490/491 licensee monitoring; staff with 20 contact hours in an APD-approved curriculum (or RBT, or 90 classroom hours of ABA), APD-approved emergency procedures training, monthly competency monitoring of 50% of staff and yearly recertification [S5].
- **Weekly staffing schedule** posted one week ahead; actual schedules kept six months (65G-2.008(6)) [S15].

### Training
| Requirement | Timing | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Zero Tolerance (abuse/neglect/exploitation) | Before providing services; every 3 years | [S15][S5] |
| Direct Care Core Competencies | Within 90 days | [S15][S5] |
| Classroom first aid + CPR (no online-only) | Within 90 days; one CPR-certified staff on site whenever residents are present | [S15] |
| HIV/AIDS | Within 90 days | [S15] |
| Emergency management plan | Within 30 days of hire; annually | [S17] |
| Medication administration (unlicensed staff) | APD Basic Medication Administration course (≥85% exam, 100% MAR section) + validation; annual update and revalidation | [S29] |
| Residents' behavior plans | Trained by a certified behavior analyst | [S15] |

### Required systems and records
- **APD iConnect** — APD's data system for documentation and authorizations; EVV in iConnect applies to personal care and home health, not residential habilitation [S5].
- Census changes reported to APD in writing before the change; updated census within five calendar days (65G-2.006(2)) [S12].
- Resident records kept six years; copies to APD within two days on request (65G-2.009(5)) [S16].
- Annual sex-offender registry check within one mile; annual driving-history checks for drivers (65G-2.008(4)) [S15].
- Monthly fire drills (not between midnight and 5 a.m.) and an annual CEMP update (65G-2.010) [S17].
- Personal needs allowance and resident funds accounting (65G-2.009(4), 65G-2.018) [S16][S19].
- An implementation plan per resident and quarterly summaries/annual report to the support coordinator [S5].
sections.market_conditions:
### Supply
No official count of APD-licensed group homes or beds was found, and this report does not estimate one. APD reports 6,639 monthly residential habilitation users in June 2026 [S24].

### Rates
Residential habilitation rates were flat from July 1, 2024 through the October 1, 2025 table [S4][S1]. The July 2026 table adds about 1.0% (e.g., Moderate $5,058.37 → $5,108.95) and is in rule development [S3][S55]. Rates do not vary by home size, so larger homes earn more per dollar of fixed cost [S1].

### Wages (BLS/O*NET 2025, Florida)
- Personal care aides (from home health and personal care aides): 10th percentile $14.74, median **$16.25**, 75th $17.25; metro medians Miami-Fort Lauderdale-West Palm Beach $15.81, Orlando $16.40, Tampa $16.45, Jacksonville $16.53 [S31].
- Social and community service managers: median $76,050 (Miami $79,240; Tampa $77,560; Jacksonville $75,660; Orlando $75,250) [S32].
- Medical secretaries/administrative assistants: median $41,730 [S33].
- RNs $40.48; LPNs $29.70 (median) [S34].

Florida's minimum wage rose to **$15.00/hour on September 30, 2026** [S35][S36]. The 10th-percentile aide wage ($14.74) is now below the legal floor, and the median is only $1.25 above it — expect wage pressure.

### Employer costs
Employer FICA 7.65% [S40]; Florida reemployment tax 2.7% new-employer rate on the first $7,000 [S38][S39]; FUTA [S41]; workers' compensation mandatory at four or more employees [S37].

### Housing
HUD FY2027 Small Area FMRs: Orlando-area ZIP 32825 3BR $2,580 and 4BR $3,020 [S44]; Fort Lauderdale-area ZIP 33024 3BR $2,990 and 4BR $3,450 [S45]. FMRs are a benchmark for ordinary rentals; landlords may charge more for group-home use.
sections.financial_narrative:
**How the model works.** Revenue per resident = the October 1, 2025 monthly residential habilitation rate for each support level in the mix (agency, non-geographical) [S1] plus room and board at APD's **$583.42** standard [S26]. Direct-care staffing has two parts. **(1) A fixed 24/7 floor:** 730 hours a month per home (one staff member on duty 24 hours × 30.42 days), because at least one staff person must be present whenever residents are home (65G-2.009(6)(b)) [S16]; this cost starts with the first admission and does not shrink while the home fills. **(2) A per-resident line for the handbook hours above that floor:** the handbook minimum for the mix at full census (Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8 hours per resident per day × 30.42) [S5], minus the floor, spread over the licensed beds — 71.03 h per resident-month for the 6-bed home, 91.25 h for the 8-bed homes and 121.65 h for the behavior-focus home. At full census the two parts equal the handbook minimum exactly; at 93% occupancy they carry about 51 hours per home per month more than the strict per-resident minimum, because vacancy trims only the per-resident part (a conservative simplification worth about $970 per home per month). The 3- and 4-resident homes carry only the 730-hour floor, which already exceeds their handbook minimum. DSPs are paid the Florida aide median **$16.25** [S31] ($17.25 in behavior-focus homes, including a $1.00 operator-estimate premium). Every configuration pays a facility operator/program director (Florida median $76,050 × FTE) [S32][S14] and a billing/office coordinator ($41,730 × FTE) [S33]. Payroll burden is 17.3%: taxes 8.3% (FICA plus reemployment tax and FUTA on the first $7,000) [S40][S38][S41], workers' comp 4% and benefits 5% (operator estimates). Rent (HUD SAFMR) [S44], utilities, vehicles and insurance are **fixed per home**. Default occupancy is 93% (88% conservative, 97% optimistic) — an operator assumption.

**Results at 93% occupancy (monthly).**
- **3-resident foster home, Live-In rate:** revenue $13,522, expenses $22,869, **−$9,347**. The Live-In rate ($140.14/day) cannot pay round-the-clock shift staff; it works only with a live-in caregiver.
- **4-bed group home:** revenue $21,042, expenses $23,241, **−$2,199**; break-even needs more than 100% occupancy. With an unpaid owner-operator it is about −$340.
- **6-bed group home:** revenue $33,159, expenses $34,246, **−$1,087**; break-even occupancy about 97%. If the owner is the unpaid facility operator, about +$2,630.
- **8-bed group home:** revenue $42,084, expenses $40,829, **+$1,255 (3.0%)**; break-even occupancy about 89%.
- **8-bed behavior-focus home:** revenue $50,499, expenses $48,558, **+$1,941 (3.8%)** after a $1,500/month BCBA contract and the wage premium; break-even about 87%.
- **Two 8-bed homes (default):** revenue $84,167, expenses $81,304, **+$2,864 (3.4%)**, about $34,000 a year; break-even occupancy about 88%; at 88% occupancy about +$50.

**Ramp-up and year 1.** The model admits 1 resident a month in the 3–6 bed homes, 2 a month in the 8-bed homes and 3 a month across the two-home model (operator estimates), while the 24/7 floor is paid from day one. Year-1 net: 6-bed −$71,500; 8-bed −$24,200; behavior-focus 8-bed −$20,500; two 8-bed homes opened together −$80,100 (first profitable month: month 4 for the 8-bed homes, month 6 for the two-home model; the 3–6 bed homes never reach a profitable month at 93%). Peak cumulative operating deficit: 8-bed about $35,500, behavior-focus about $38,000, two-home about $100,200, 6-bed about $97,600. Cash needed = one-time startup costs plus the larger of that deficit or APD's 60-day financial-ability reserve (65G-2.0032(5)) [S11]: about $134,600 for one 8-bed home and $245,900 for two. None of the configurations recovers startup costs plus the ramp-up deficit within 36 months at default assumptions. **Opening the second home only after the first is full** avoids paying a second empty-home floor (about $13,900 a month in wages and burden) during the ramp and cuts the two-home deficit substantially.

**Sensitivities (default two-home model unless noted).**
- **Wages:** at the 75th-percentile aide wage of $17.25 the default loses about $440; at $18.00 it loses about $2,920. The break-even DSP wage is about **$17.10**. The 6-bed home loses about $2,410 at $17.25.
- **Staffing above the minimum:** 10% more direct-care hours than the handbook minimum turns the default to about −$2,310 and the 8-bed home to about −$1,330. Most homes staff above the minimum for overnight and weekend coverage, so this is the biggest risk.
- **Strict per-resident minimum:** if staffing tracked the handbook minimum for residents actually present (never below the 24/7 floor) instead of the conservative floor-plus-line simplification, steady-state results would be about $970 per home per month better (default about +$4,810; 8-bed about +$2,230; 6-bed about −$110).
- **Room and board:** if residents can pay $815.08 (SSI minus the PNA) instead of $583.42 — not established in rule — the default rises to about +$6,310.
- **July 2026 rates (+1.0%):** about +$3,620 for the default and −$790 for the 6-bed home [S55].
- **Owner as program director (unpaid):** the default rises to about +$10,300; the 8-bed home to about +$4,970.
- **South Florida 6-bed home:** at geographical rates (+7.5%) and a Broward 4BR rent of $3,450 [S45], about +$730 at a $16.25 wage, or about −$500 at the Miami 75th-percentile aide wage of $17.18 [S31].
- **10-bed home** (2 Minimal, 5 Moderate, 3 Extensive 1; rent at 1.4 × the 4BR SAFMR, 0.6 FTE program director, operator estimates): about +$3,370.

The model counts no add-on revenue (residential nursing, transportation) and no startup interest.
sections.risks:
- **Thin margin on staffing.** The rates fund roughly $28 per required staff hour. Staffing 10% above the handbook minimum, or paying about $0.85/hour above the $16.25 median, erases the default profit [S5][S31]. Residents' real needs, overnight coverage and the rule that one staff is present whenever residents are home (65G-2.009(6)(b)) push hours above the minimum [S16].
- **Minimum wage.** Florida's $15.00 floor (Sept. 30, 2026) is close to market DSP pay; competition for staff will raise wages [S35][S31].
- **Zoning for 7–14 beds.** Larger homes must be in multifamily zoning and can be denied within 1,200 ft of another community residential home or 500 ft of single-family zoning [S25]; APD's own siting rule caps three facilities within 1,000 ft [S18]. The profitable 8-bed configurations depend on finding a compliant site.
- **Support level changes.** Rates follow each resident's APD-assigned level; a downgrade cuts revenue immediately, and Extensive staffing reductions need APD written approval [S1][S5].
- **Vacancy and absences.** Fewer than 24 days in the home drops a resident to the daily rate, and empty beds earn nothing [S1][S5].
- **Flat rates.** Residential habilitation rates did not change from July 2024 to October 2025; the July 2026 increase is only about 1% [S4][S3].
- **Room and board.** The model assumes $583.42; residents' benefits, representative-payee duties and the PNA limit what can be collected [S19][S26].
- **Regulatory actions.** APD monitors monthly; violations can lead to fines, conditional licenses, denial or revocation (65G-2.004–2.005) [S22][S30]. A late renewal is treated as an initial application [S9].
- **Abuse findings.** A verified finding against staff requires supervision restrictions and a corrective action plan within 15 days (65G-2.008(5)) [S15].
- **Hurricanes.** The CEMP must cover evacuation and sheltering; facilities must evacuate when directed (65G-2.010) [S17].
- **Financial ability.** APD may require proof that you can operate 60 days without state payments (65G-2.0032(5)) [S11].
- **Cash flow.** Monthly billing is submitted only after the month ends [S5], so plan for at least two months of payroll before the first payment. The 24/7 staffing floor is paid from the first admission, so year 1 loses money in every configuration (two 8-bed homes opened together: about −$80,000).
sections.recommendations:
1. **Plan for 8 beds per home, or several homes.** At current rates a 6-bed home loses about $1,100/month with a paid program director; 8-bed homes earn about $1,250–$1,950/month each [S1][S5]. If you start with one 6-bed home, plan to be the unpaid facility operator yourself until a second home opens.
2. **Find a site that fits s. 419.001 before anything else.** For 7–14 residents, look in multifamily zones away from single-family zoning (500 ft) and other community residential homes (1,200 ft); confirm in writing with the local zoning office before signing a lease [S25][S18].
3. **Start Level 2 screening and APD enrollment early.** Send the Clearinghouse Letter of Intent and APD application while you search for property; you need the Provider Service Listing Letter before Medicaid enrollment [S21][S23].
4. **Staff to the residents' handbook minimum, flexibly.** Concentrate staff when residents are home (evenings, weekends) and reduce while they attend ADT or work, as the handbook allows [S5]. Track hours per resident per day weekly against the minimum.
5. **Admit a balanced mix.** Moderate and Extensive 1 residents pay more in absolute dollars; per required staff hour, all standard levels pay about the same. Choose residents whose needs your staffing pattern can meet without overtime.
6. **Consider behavior-focus designation once experienced.** It adds about 4–5% per resident but needs a BCBA contract, trained staff and APD designation [S5][S1].
7. **Use APD's room-and-board process.** File Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days for residents under 22 or with low benefits [S27].
8. **Watch the July 2026 rate table** (about +1.0%) and APD provider advisories [S3].
9. **Budget cash for the ramp-up.** Keep at least 60 days of operating costs available (APD can ask for proof) plus the ramp-up deficit [S11]. One staff must be on duty 24/7 from the first admission (65G-2.009(6)(b)) [S16], so open the second home only after the first is nearly full — opening both together roughly doubles the empty-home staffing cost during ramp-up.

checklist.task: Confirm the right license: APD group home or foster care facility (not an AHCA ALF)
checklist.instructions: DD group homes are licensed by APD under s. 393.067 and ch. 65G-2. Group home = 4–15 residents; foster care facility = up to 3. APD will not fund an unlicensed facility. Residential habilitation centers (9+) are not an option: no new licenses since Oct. 1, 1989 (s. 393.063(35)).

checklist.task: Choose your service tier
checklist.instructions: Standard residential habilitation is the entry point. Behavior focus, intensive behavioral and enhanced intensive behavioral require APD designation and extra staff qualifications. The Live-In rate applies only to homes licensed for three or fewer.

checklist.task: Form a Florida LLC or corporation
checklist.instructions: File Articles of Organization on Sunbiz ($100) plus registered agent designation ($25). Annual report $138.75, due Jan. 1–May 1; $400 late fee after May 1 [S53]. The entity name must match on the APD and Medicaid applications.
checklist.cite: s. 605.0213, F.S.; Sunbiz annual report fees

checklist.task: Get county (and city) local business tax receipts for each home
checklist.instructions: Apply with the county tax collector and, inside city limits, the city; fees vary (operator estimate about $50–$300 per home per year) and renew annually.

checklist.task: Obtain an EIN
checklist.instructions: Apply free at irs.gov. The license application asks for the FEIN.

checklist.task: Open a business bank account and document financial ability
checklist.instructions: APD requires satisfactory proof of financial ability to operate and may request proof you can operate 60 days without state payment (bank statements, line of credit).

checklist.task: Read the iBudget handbook and the rate table
checklist.instructions: Read residential habilitation (pp. 2-46–2-65), qualifications and Appendix B training. Note the minimum staff hours per level and the monthly (24+ days) vs daily billing rule.

checklist.task: Build your budget with the APD Annual Budget Sheet
checklist.instructions: The license application requires a projected 12-month budget (income by licensed capacity, personnel, workers' comp, transportation, liability insurance, supplies). Use this bundle's P&L.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Decide home size against zoning rules
checklist.instructions: Six or fewer residents = single-family use, no local approval unless within 1,000 ft of another such home or 1,200 ft of a community residential home. 7–14 residents must be in multifamily zoning; local government can approve, deny (within 60 days) or not respond.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Check distance limits
checklist.instructions: APD: no more than three facilities within 1,000 ft; within 1,000 ft requires a local variance. For 7–14 beds, a site within 1,200 ft of another community residential home or 500 ft of single-family zoning can be denied.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Complete the zoning notification steps
checklist.instructions: Print FloridaHealthFinder proximity searches (ALF, AFCH, residential treatment, ICF/DD within one mile), get DCF and APD lists of nearby community residential homes, give them to local zoning, and notify zoning once the home receives its first resident.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Secure the home (lease or purchase)
checklist.instructions: APD asks that the home be secured before you request an application. A fully executed lease is required if you rent. Mobile/manufactured homes are not allowed.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Verify bedroom capacity
checklist.instructions: Max two residents per bedroom (homes first licensed on/after 7/1/2014); single rooms ≥80 sq ft, shared ≥60 sq ft per person; direct access from a common area; staff-only bedrooms do not count.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Verify bathrooms and living space
checklist.instructions: One toilet, sink and tub/shower per three residents; 35 sq ft of living/dining space per household member; ventilation; accessible design for residents' disabilities.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Install safety items
checklist.instructions: Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors; hot water ≤120°F at outlets; heating/cooling; restrict access to pools/water hazards; secure hazardous chemicals; no portable heaters in bedrooms (≤6 residents).

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Furnish bedrooms and common areas
checklist.instructions: Bed, dresser/chest, shelf space, window coverings, linens; let residents decorate. Designate an office area with secure records storage.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Confirm HCBS settings compliance
checklist.instructions: Provider-controlled settings need a lease or equivalent agreement, lockable bedroom doors, roommate choice, access to food and visitors, freedom to decorate.

checklist.phase: PHASE 2 — SITE SELECTION, ZONING & PHYSICAL PLANT
checklist.task: Do not schedule a DOH group care inspection
checklist.instructions: The Department of Health states it does not inspect APD-licensed homes. (The old checklist required one.)

checklist.task: Request Clearinghouse access (Letter of Intent)
checklist.instructions: If you lack an "APD General" eligibility determination, send the Provider Applicant Access Request to your region's Intent mailbox ([region].Intent@apdcares.org).

checklist.task: Register in the Clearinghouse and get fingerprinted
checklist.instructions: Register 5–10 business days after the request; use a Clearinghouse-authorized Livescan vendor. Do nothing else until results clear (Northeast Region guidance).

checklist.task: Screen all owners, managers and staff
checklist.instructions: The applicant, managers, supervisors and every direct service staff member need Level 2 screening before licensure; sign the screening affidavit.

checklist.task: Name a qualified facility operator and backup
checklist.instructions: Operator: 90 college credits in a related field or high school diploma + 3 years' disability experience; on site or on call at all times; designate a backup for absences.

checklist.task: Line up a behavior analyst (if behavior focus)
checklist.instructions: A BCBA or Ch. 490/491 licensee at Level 1/2 must monitor behavior programs face to face. Get a written contract.

checklist.task: Check disqualifying history
checklist.instructions: APD weighs prior disciplinary actions, revocations, bankruptcy, verified abuse findings and good moral character.

checklist.task: Complete the APD iBudget provider application
checklist.instructions: After screening clears, complete the application for residential habilitation with the agency checklist documents and Clearinghouse printout. Incomplete packets are not processed.

checklist.task: Submit policies and procedures with the packet
checklist.instructions: Agency applicants must submit policies and procedures; all checklist documents go in at one time. Request the checklist from your region's provider enrollment email.

checklist.task: Submit to your regional provider enrollment specialist
checklist.instructions: Email [region].providerenrollment@apdcares.org. Packets are reviewed in the order received. There is no fee.

checklist.task: Receive the iBudget Provider Service Listing Letter
checklist.instructions: APD issues a draft listing letter if you are eligible; you need it for Medicaid enrollment.

checklist.task: Request behavior-focus or intensive-behavior designation (if applicable)
checklist.instructions: These services may only be provided in homes APD designates.

checklist.task: Write behavioral intervention and sexual activity policies
checklist.instructions: Required attachments to the license application.

checklist.task: Write admission and termination criteria
checklist.instructions: Required for group home applications. Serve only residents whose characteristics, level of care, age and sex match the license.

checklist.task: Prepare the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP)
checklist.instructions: Use APD's CEMP template; cover evacuation, sheltering, staffing, post-disaster needs; update annually; attach any local approval letter.

checklist.task: Write video monitoring criteria (if cameras used)
checklist.instructions: Written criteria for which residents are monitored; never use footage to humiliate or punish.

checklist.task: Set up resident funds and PNA procedures
checklist.instructions: As representative payee, set aside at least 18% of the SSI federal benefit rate ($178.92 in 2026) as personal needs allowance; keep separate accounting.

checklist.task: Write medication administration procedures
checklist.instructions: Unlicensed staff may administer medication only after APD's Basic Medication Administration course and validation; revalidate annually.

checklist.task: Buy liability, auto and workers' comp insurance
checklist.instructions: No minimum limit was found in rule; get quotes. Workers' comp is mandatory with four or more employees. Drivers need valid licenses and annual driving-history checks.

checklist.task: Prepare personnel policies and job descriptions
checklist.instructions: Job descriptions, training records, personnel files with screening, weekly schedules one week ahead (keep six months).

checklist.phase: PHASE 6 — FIRE INSPECTION & APD FACILITY LICENSE
checklist.task: Pass the fire inspection
checklist.instructions: Request inspection by the local fire authority or State Fire Marshal under ch. 69A-38. An approved inspection is required before the initial license and every renewal.

checklist.phase: PHASE 6 — FIRE INSPECTION & APD FACILITY LICENSE
checklist.task: Submit APD Application Request and interview
checklist.instructions: Submit the Application Request with photo ID once the home is secured; APD regional staff will interview you.

checklist.phase: PHASE 6 — FIRE INSPECTION & APD FACILITY LICENSE
checklist.task: Submit License Application Form 65G-2.002-A (December 2025)
checklist.instructions: Select Initial and Group Home (or Foster Care). Attach articles, staff information, marketing materials, lease, fire inspection, CEMP, financial ability, Annual Budget Sheet, policies, floor plan, admission criteria, zoning documentation. No license fee appears on the form.

checklist.phase: PHASE 6 — FIRE INSPECTION & APD FACILITY LICENSE
checklist.task: Request the capacity and resident characteristics you want
checklist.instructions: APD sets licensed capacity from residents' needs, staffing, operator qualifications, services and fire limits.

checklist.phase: PHASE 6 — FIRE INSPECTION & APD FACILITY LICENSE
checklist.task: Pass the APD licensure inspection
checklist.instructions: APD will not schedule it until documents and screenings are complete. Deficiencies must be corrected before the license issues. Respond within 21 days if APD writes by regular mail after certified mail fails.

checklist.phase: PHASE 6 — FIRE INSPECTION & APD FACILITY LICENSE
checklist.task: Receive the one-year license
checklist.instructions: The license is valid for the dates shown; each home has its own license.

checklist.task: Enroll in Florida Medicaid
checklist.instructions: Use the Medicaid Provider Enrollment Wizard; upload the APD listing letter. Medicaid runs its own screening review. The CY 2026 federal application fee is $750 where it applies — confirm.

checklist.task: Receive the Medicaid Welcome Letter and send it to APD
checklist.instructions: The letter contains your Medicaid provider ID; send a copy to your Regional Provider Enrollment Specialist.

checklist.task: Sign the Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement (MWSA)
checklist.instructions: AHCA Form 5000-3553, signed with APD, completes enrollment.

checklist.task: Set up APD iConnect access
checklist.instructions: Complete APD iConnect training (≥75% test) to get access for documentation and billing.

checklist.task: Hire qualified DSPs
checklist.instructions: 18+, high school diploma/GED, Level 2 screening, one year of relevant experience or 30 semester hours/720 classroom hours; or use the 90-day supervised alternative with notice to APD within 5 days and a 120-day evaluation.

checklist.task: Plan staffing to the handbook minimum and the supervision rule
checklist.instructions: Minimum direct-care hours per resident per day: Minimal 4, Moderate 6, Extensive 1 8, Extensive 2 11 (sum for the home, meet daily or weekly). Always one staff present when residents are home.

checklist.task: Zero Tolerance training before work
checklist.instructions: All DSPs before providing services; refresher every three years.

checklist.task: Direct Care Core Competencies within 90 days
checklist.instructions: APD curriculum; web-based course available.

checklist.task: Classroom CPR and first aid within 90 days
checklist.instructions: Online-only courses are not acceptable; at least one CPR-certified staff on site whenever residents are present.

checklist.task: HIV/AIDS course within 90 days
checklist.instructions: All staff.

checklist.task: Medication administration certification
checklist.instructions: APD Basic Medication Administration course and validation by an approved validator; annual update and revalidation within 60 days before expiry.

checklist.task: Emergency plan training within 30 days of hire
checklist.instructions: Train all staff on the CEMP within 30 days and annually.

checklist.task: Behavior-focus staff training (if applicable)
checklist.instructions: 20 contact hours in an APD-approved curriculum (or RBT or 90 classroom ABA hours) plus APD-approved emergency procedures training; yearly recertification.

checklist.task: Get referrals from support coordinators and APD
checklist.instructions: Waiver Support Coordinators authorize services; APD regional offices place crisis cases.

checklist.task: Wait for service authorizations before serving
checklist.instructions: Bill only services covered by a WSC-issued authorization.

checklist.task: Report census changes to APD
checklist.instructions: Notify APD in writing before a census change; send the updated census within five calendar days.

checklist.task: Write an implementation plan for each resident
checklist.instructions: Developed with the resident and tied to support plan goals; file quarterly summaries and the annual report.
checklist.cite: iBudget Handbook (Implementation Plan, Quarterly Summary definitions; p. 2-48)

checklist.task: Prepare for the 30-day post-admission APD review
checklist.instructions: APD reviews the home on site within 30 days after the first admission.

checklist.task: Bill correctly: monthly vs daily
checklist.instructions: Monthly rate at 24+ days in the home; daily rate otherwise; submit after month end; never bill days the resident was absent.

checklist.task: Claim APD room-and-board payments where eligible
checklist.instructions: Form 65G-13.008A within 90 days after month end; $583.42 for residents under 22, shortfall for low-benefit adults.

checklist.task: Notify local zoning that the home is licensed
checklist.instructions: After the license, notify zoning once the home receives its first resident.

checklist.task: Renew each license 45+ days before expiration
checklist.instructions: Late or incomplete renewals become initial applications.

checklist.task: Annual fire inspection
checklist.instructions: Request annually; needed for renewal.

checklist.task: Monthly fire drills and annual CEMP update
checklist.instructions: No drills between midnight and 5 a.m.

checklist.task: Expect monthly APD monitoring
checklist.instructions: At least monthly visits, one on a weekend each year; allow inspection and copies of records.

checklist.task: Annual sex-offender and driving checks
checklist.instructions: Check the FDLE registry within one mile and notify staff; update drivers' histories annually.

checklist.task: Report abuse immediately
checklist.instructions: Call the Florida Abuse Hotline 1-800-962-2873; follow investigation rules for staff named as alleged perpetrators.

checklist.task: Track Level 2 rescreening and training expirations
checklist.instructions: Zero Tolerance every 3 years; med admin annually; CPR per card.

checklist.task: File annual cost statement and LLC annual report
checklist.instructions: Each licensed facility must file an annual sworn statement of its costs of caring for APD-funded clients (s. 393.067(10)). File the Sunbiz LLC annual report ($138.75) between Jan. 1 and May 1 to avoid the $400 late fee [S53].

checklist.task: Give 30 days' notice before closing a home
checklist.instructions: Written notice to APD.

checklist.task: Request capacity changes 30 days ahead
checklist.instructions: Include a passed fire inspection and zoning compliance.

checklist.task: Watch rate table updates
checklist.instructions: The July 2026 table (about +1%) is in rulemaking; check Rule 59G-13.081.

corrections_vs_previous: The old checklist required a Department of Health environmental health inspection under ch. 64E-12 (and a food permit under 64E-11). DOH states it does not conduct any inspections at APD-licensed homes [S28].

The old checklist said to "submit required application fees" that "vary by home size/region." No APD license fee appears on Form 65G-2.002-A or APD's Group Homes page, and APD states waiver enrollment is free [S20][S21].

The old checklist cited Rule 65G-2.012 for group home standards and floor plans; it was transferred on 7/1/2014 and group home standards are now Rule 65G-2.0072, with physical standards in 65G-2.007 (both amended 3/26/2026) [S30].

The old checklist cited s. 429.435, F.S. (an assisted living statute) for fire safety; APD homes are inspected under ch. 69A-38 per Rule 65G-2.010(2), before the initial license and every renewal [S17].

The old checklist said to "apply through APD iConnect" for an iBudget provider number in 1–2 weeks. The real sequence is Clearinghouse screening → APD application → Provider Service Listing Letter → Medicaid Provider Enrollment Wizard → Welcome Letter → Medicaid Waiver Services Agreement; no processing time is published [S21].

The old checklist did not mention that homes of 7–14 residents must be in multifamily zoning and can be denied within 1,200 ft of another community residential home or 500 ft of single-family zoning, or APD's three-facilities-within-1,000-ft limit [S25][S18].
The old checklist did not cover the handbook's minimum direct-care staff hours by support level, the one-staff-present rule, or the operator qualifications (65G-2.0072) [S5][S16][S14].

The old checklist's "APD Attachment 9 Facility Form", "Affidavit of Good Moral Character notarization" and "COI listing APD as certificate holder" steps could not be verified in the current Form 65G-2.002-A or rules and were omitted.
